Accrual and cash-basis accounting differ in when you record income and expenses.

- Cash basis: you record income when money actually arrives and record expenses when you actually pay. It’s simple and shows your cash on hand.

- Accrual basis: you record income when you earn it (for example, when you deliver a product or complete a service), even if the customer pays later. You record expenses when they are incurred (for example, when you get a bill), even if you pay it later. This matches revenue and the costs that created it, so it shows whether the business actually made or lost money over a period.

Which to use: cash is easier and reflects actual cash flow; accrual gives a more accurate picture of ongoing performance, especially if you have invoicing, inventory, or delayed payments.
